headline: Agentic AI Raises the Stakes on Campus Security
thesis: A new Inside Higher Ed column warns of AI-enabled attacks after "Black October," while teachers redesign assessment for an age when the take-home essay no longer works.
summary: Inside Higher Ed's Ray Schroeder argues higher ed has entered an era of agentic, AI-enabled cyberattacks and must be ready to respond within minutes, on the heels of the claimed Vanderbilt ransomware breach. THE Journal adds that 84% of organizations logged an AI-related incident this year while governance lags. In classrooms, an EdSurge teacher essay describes retiring the take-home essay for live, defended work, and EdSurge asks how schools can teach voting without partisanship. EdTech Magazine covers a Hanover report showing AI use outpacing guidance, and Brookings makes the case for student AI councils.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 12, 2026 · Built from search results only; direct site fetches were blocked in this environment, so some sources show recent or evergreen items rather than items dated today.
